body:
It would seem that this is quite a fundamental problem.

Since patch exports are based off of some exported main pack, which will include `.remap` files that (in this case) map `main.tscn` to `.godot/exported/**-main.scn`, you will when exporting said patch end up omitting the `.remap` file for `main.tscn`, since the `.remap` file technically hasn't changed from the exported main pack.

This means that when you go to load `main.tscn` in a non-exported scenario, it will find no `.remap` file and thereby fall back on loading the normal path, which will go through the regular platform `FileAccess` and load the old `main.tscn` that's on disk, as opposed to the `main.scn` in the PCK.

In other words, a patch PCK is essentially a diff based on an exported build, which means it's not really applicable to a non-exported build.

---

I guess one crude solution could be to forcefully include any relevant `.remap` files when creating patch exports. That would however bloat the patches for the only purpose of supporting loading them in a non-exported build.

> I guess one crude solution could be to forcefully include any relevant `.remap` files when creating patch exports. That would however bloat the patches for the only purpose of supporting loading them in a non-exported build.

Even just trying this turned out to be a headache, due to how the hash check for patched files, which can be found in [`EditorExportPlatform::_save_pack_patch_file`](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/394508d26dcf1b7a9362453f9009c07d969f1a7e/editor/export/editor_export_platform.cpp#L342), is separated from the only place where all the remaps are known, which is in [`EditorExportPlatform::export_project_files`](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/394508d26dcf1b7a9362453f9009c07d969f1a7e/editor/export/editor_export_platform.cpp#L1531-L1546).

It might technically be possible to parse the `*.remap` files in `EditorExportPlatform::_save_pack_patch_file` as they're coming in, in order to check if the mapped-to file has already been exported, but that would frankly be a hack on so many levels that I don't think it's worth it, especially considering that the desired outcome is questionable to begin with.

Since I don't see any other way to "fix" this, and with the current behavior making some kind of sense, I'll go ahead and drop the severity on this and leave it for now, and we'll just have to see if more people stumble onto this quirk.
It seems that the editor listens for file changes in real time and refreshes the content, so files loaded with pck are always considered too long and refreshed

You are likely talking about a different issue, @Esual. This issue has to do with how patch PCKs in particular are exported, i.e. the ones you get if you rely on the "Patches" tab in the export dialog, where you only end up exporting the difference from the PCKs listed there.

i am having some confusing feedback about the `replace_files` parameter in `ProjectSettings.load_resource_pack()` that may be related to this issue
this is reproduced in 4.4.1
this is my script, which is in my main scene:

```swift
# CONSTANTS
const mods_path: String = "user://mods"



func _unhandled_input(event: InputEvent) -> void:
    if event.is_action_pressed("replace_files"):
        load_mods(true)
    elif event.is_action_pressed("do_not_replace_files"):
        load_mods(false)



func load_mods(replace_files: bool) -> void:
    print("Replace files? %s" % replace_files)
    
    var dir: DirAccess = DirAccess.open(mods_path)
    if dir:
        var files: PackedStringArray = dir.get_files()
        
        for file_path in files:
            var success: bool = ProjectSettings.load_resource_pack(
                    "%s/%s" % [mods_path, file_path],
                    replace_files
            )
            print("Success: %s - on mod '%s'" % [success, file_path])
    else:
        print("NO MOD FOLDER, PROBABLY")
    
    print("MOVING TO THE MOD SCENE...")
    await get_tree().process_frame 
    get_tree().change_scene_to_file("res://mod_scene.tscn")
```
`mod_scene.tscn` is a simple scene containing a `Sprite2D` which i change the `self_modulate` of to simulate changes.
essentially, the behavior of the moddable project seems to change depending on what was most recently exported:
1. i change the `self_modulate`
2. i export a pack (this pack includes `mod_scene.tscn` and no other resources)
3. i return the `self_modulate` to how it was before
4. i run the game in the editor and try both 'replace files' and 'do not replace'. both sprites are not modulated (expected).
5. i move the `.pck` mod to the mods folder
6. 'replace files' and 'do not replace' sprites are now modulated (unexpected). 
7. i export the project completely, then run it from the editor (nothing else has changed)
8. now the settings behave how i would expect. that is:
* 'replace files' will cause the mod to be loaded, making the sprite modulated
* 'do not replace' will cause the mod to not load, making the sprite normal

the enclosed `.zip` is the project folder. 

if you run the game as an executable, rather than from the editor, you do not have this problem. at least, that is the behavior from my end. 

[mod-testing.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24249399/mod-testing.zip)
